facts.text: Cash generation is strong but is flattered by customer funding. facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest case against the comfortable reading is the Philadelphia hotel litigation: the court awarded the developer approximately USD 175 million, the company's building subsidiary has appealed, and management describes a material adverse impact as neither probable nor remote, against USD 504,218 thousand of general-purpose cash. A second weakness is the earnings record, since FY2024 EBITDA was negative and FY2025 EBITDA includes USD 150,002 thousand of share-based compensation that moves with the share price. The view would turn if the award were upheld in full on appeal, if billings in excess of costs fell while backlog shrank, or if cash available for general corporate purposes fell back toward the USD 265,647 thousand of FY2024. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tpc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 10, 25–26; 10-K_2025-12-31_tpc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 78; calculation C19

facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest evidence against a moderate governance risk reading is the covenant record and the dispute record: the first lien leverage covenant needed two amendments within five months in 2022 and 2023, FY2024 ended in a loss with legacy-dispute charges, and a court awarded approximately USD 175 million, equal to 34.71% of the USD 504,218 thousand of general-purpose cash. The strongest evidence for the opposite, a lower-risk reading, is that distributions were only 6.20% of nine-month 2026 operating cash flow and that the 2026 refinancing lowered interest cost and extended maturity without any documented priming. The view would worsen if the appeal fails and the award is paid from general-purpose cash, if the indenture or credit agreement prove to allow large restricted payments, or if repurchases accelerate while backlog keeps falling. It would improve if the documents show tight restricted-payment limits and the appeal reduces the award. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_tpc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 26; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tpc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 10, 25–26; calculation C7; calculation C8; calculation C13

facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: The only new debt issue in the period is the refinancing completed on 2026-07-02. facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: The business profile is adequate: large and scaled in work where few firms compete, but concentrated in a handful of big fixed-price public projects. Last-twelve-months revenue is USD 6,254,126 thousand, public agencies were 73.82% of nine-month 2026 revenue, and two customers with multiple projects made up 24.1% of it, at 13.3% and 10.8%; the third-quarter report names the second customer, so the earlier Business & governance figure of one customer at 10.8% understates concentration. Management says fewer firms now bid on the largest civil projects, which helps pricing but cannot be tested because no market-share figure is supplied. A funding delay or a dispute on one large project therefore moves earnings and cash more than the revenue base suggests, so scale is a strength and concentration is the matching weakness. facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Revenue is visible for about three years, but the pipeline that feeds it has stopped growing. Nine-month 2026 new awards of USD 4,540.3 million were 0.96x revenue recognised, against USD 7.0 billion in the same period of 2025, and backlog is down 5.77% on a year earlier although up from USD 19.9 billion at the end of the second quarter. Firm remaining performance obligations, which exclude unexercised options, are USD 17.4 billion, 2.78x revenue and down only 2.79% on a year earlier, so the firm base is steadier than the headline backlog. Management attributes the fall to an unusually strong 2025 and fewer large awards reaching decision in 2026, and points to a pipeline above USD 200 billion over three to four years and a multi-billion-dollar California healthcare project to be added within two years; these are expectations, not bookings. Backlog equal to 3.25 years of revenue protects earnings in the near term, but sustained awards below revenue would shrink it and the customer advances attached to it. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tpc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 8, 49–50, 52–53, 58; calculation C6; calculation C7; calculation C9

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Disputes are a recurring cost of this business model, not a one-off, and unproven claims decide how much profit turns into cash. Legal judgments and settlements cost USD 213.5 million in FY2024 and USD 94.3 million in FY2025, which is 40.65% of FY2025 income from construction operations, and a USD 16.4 million adverse change on a California transit project in the first quarter of 2026 came from change-order negotiations that management says were later settled with the owner and should bring cash. Fixed-price work was 79% of backlog at the end of 2025, and claims plus unapproved change orders of USD 687,916 thousand are 89.64% of the USD 767,432 thousand of costs in excess of billings and 136.43% of general-purpose cash, with management expecting about USD 521.4 million of that balance to be collected beyond one year, so a lost claim becomes a charge and a delayed collection together. The third-quarter report states this split, which corrects the earlier Business & governance statement that it is not stated. facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Financial policy has shifted from repair to returns, which is acceptable at this leverage but has not been tested by a downturn. The first lien leverage covenant needed two amendments in 2022 and 2023 and FY2024 ended in a loss; since then the term loan was repaid early, dividends began in December 2025 and USD 30,000 thousand of shares were bought back, leaving USD 170 million of authorisation. Returns were 6.20% of nine-month operating cash flow and gross debt is 22.69% of total capitalisation; no sponsor sits above the company, the executive chairman and related trusts hold about 12% and may nominate a director, and alignment therefore has to be judged from conduct, which so far shows returns well below operating cash flow. facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Refinancing risk is low until 2031, and the one market price supplied does not signal distress, though it is below par. The July 2026 refinancing replaced the 2029 notes with USD 400.0 million of senior unsecured notes due 2033 and lifted the secured revolver to USD 350.0 million, undrawn and maturing in 2031, at a cash premium of USD 35.6 million that the issuer-stated USD 21.0 million of annual interest saving repays in 1.70 years; management also states that interest income exceeded interest expense from the third quarter of 2026 and expects that to continue. The 2033 notes were valued at USD 390.0 million, or 97.50% of principal, at 2026-09-30, which implies a yield above the coupon, and no peer prices are supplied to say whether that is wide; the revolver's two maintenance tests, reported at -0.22x against a 3.50x maximum and 17.14x against a 3.00x minimum, apply only to the revolver and follow definitions that are not supplied. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tpc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 15–18, 34, 62, 66; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C25; calculation C26; calculation C27

facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view

facts.text: Over three to five years the outlook turns on funding that is not settled. The federal infrastructure law funding window closed on 2026-09-30 and surface-transportation authorisations were extended only to 2026-12-11 while a USD 580 billion reauthorisation bill is negotiated; management states that most major projects rely more on state and local funding, cites USD 41.4 billion of voter-approved transportation measures from November 2024, and points to defence funding in Guam and the Indo-Pacific. facts.label: Outlook, tailwinds and headwinds
facts.text: Competitive and cost forces matter to creditors mainly through bidding and margin. Management says few firms bid on the largest fixed-price civil projects, which supports awards and pricing, while customers are mostly public agencies that can end contracts for convenience and buy by competitive bid, so buyer power is high on smaller jobs and lower on the largest. Cost inflation and tariffs are managed by buying out materials, taking fixed-price quotes from subcontractors and pricing escalation into bids, which shifts much of the risk to suppliers but not all of it; about 4,000 employees are union members with wage escalation priced into bids. Technology and social factors do not appear to be a primary credit driver based on the provided materials. facts.label: Downside scenario
facts.text: The realistic downside is a loss on the Philadelphia appeal combined with awards that stay below revenue, which hits cash before it hits leverage. First, the court award of about USD 175 million and the USD 42 million window wall ruling are upheld and the share awards settle in cash, a cash call of USD 337,900 thousand that leaves USD 166,318 thousand of general-purpose cash and USD 516,318 thousand of liquidity with the revolver, and net debt on general-purpose cash of USD 237,323 thousand, or 0.60x last-twelve-months EBITDA. Second, awards below revenue stop the growth of customer advances; a return of the advances outside joint ventures to their end-2024 level would absorb a further USD 587,370 thousand, 68.76% of the original liquidity, which together with the first call, USD 925,270 thousand, would exceed the original USD 854,218 thousand of liquidity, but that needs several years of shrinking awards and is the tail, not the base case. Revenue would not fall quickly because backlog covers about three years, and margins would be pressured by further adverse adjustments like the USD 16.4 million recorded in the first quarter of 2026 and by the loss of the recovery carried on the hotel project. Management levers are the undrawn revolver, the discretionary repurchase authorisation, dividends of USD 5.0 million declared in the third quarter, the timing of equipment purchases and distributions to joint venture partners. Resilience looks sufficient to avoid liquidity distress in the first case; distress needs the combined tail, and the covenants apply only to the revolver, so a breach would first affect revolver access, and whether it would reach the notes depends on cross-default terms that are not supplied. Each 10% of claims and unapproved change orders that is not collected would cost USD 68,792 thousand of earnings and cash. These figures are arithmetic on stated amounts, not a forecast. facts.label: Overall credit view
facts.text: Overall, Tutor Perini presents an adequate business profile supported by a USD 20,353.3 million backlog, public customers and a refinanced balance sheet, but credit quality is constrained by fixed-price execution risk, recurring dispute charges and customer-funded working capital. Cash-flow durability appears adequate because operating cash flow before working capital was USD 415,231 thousand in nine months, although it is flattered by customer advances that cannot be assumed to grow. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on earnings holding near current levels and on bond market access as the 2033 notes approach maturity, since nothing of size matures sooner. The primary downside path is a loss on the Philadelphia appeal combined with awards below revenue and shrinking customer advances. Further analysis would require the executed debt documents, the covenant definitions, the collection timetable for claims and unapproved change orders, the recovery carried on the hotel project and market prices for comparison. The top risk is backlog replacement failing while claims remain uncollected. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tpc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 3, 25–26, 49–50, 66; calculation C11; calculation C7; calculation C24; calculation C17; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)

## Findings
### Bottom line

The five supplied filings are enough to support the financial foundation, business and fundamental credit work for Tutor Perini Corp, but the absence of executed debt agreements, agency ratings and dated bond quotes limits what creditors can conclude about security, covenants and pricing.

The record runs from the 2024 annual report to the quarter ended 2026-09-30, and the latest document is dated 2026-11-04, so events after that date are outside the evidence. The filings print no EBITDA, so leverage on that basis has to be built from statement lines and will not match the covenant definitions.

Executed debt agreements are not supplied. This restricts Security selection, Legal & covenants and Recovery & fulcrum, none of which this run selects.

Nothing dated after 2026-11-04 is supplied, which is 14 days before the as-of date. No later current report, earnings release, investor presentation or market update is in the evidence, so any event between those dates is not established. The third-quarter report has no separate subsequent-events note; the one post-quarter development it describes is the October 2026 ruling in which the trial court denied the company's indemnity claims against its concrete subcontractor and that subcontractor's surety in the Philadelphia hotel dispute.

No filing prints EBITDA or adjusted EBITDA. The term appears only in the credit agreement's incremental-debt basket tests, whose definition is not supplied, and the non-GAAP measures printed are adjusted net income attributable to the company and adjusted diluted earnings per share. Leverage and coverage on an EBITDA basis must be built from statement lines and will not match the covenant ratios, which the filings report only as finished ratios.

The covenant measures are not a continuous series. Through the first quarter of 2026 the revolver was tested on a maximum first lien net leverage ratio; the amended agreement replaced that test with a maximum total net leverage ratio and a minimum cash interest coverage ratio, first tested at the end of the second quarter of 2026, and the second-quarter report prints both sets of tests. Ratios reported before the amendment are therefore on a different definition from the current ones.

Reported cash includes joint venture cash. Of the cash and cash equivalents at 2026-09-30, the portion available for general corporate purposes is stated separately; the remainder is held by consolidated joint ventures and by the company's share of unconsolidated joint ventures and is available only for joint venture uses. Any liquidity or leverage view has to use the general-purpose figure, which is also the cash the covenant definitions offset against indebtedness.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tpc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 10, 63, 67; calculation C8

No agency rating, dated bond quote, peer set or portfolio limit is supplied: the run settings leave them blank and the filings mention credit ratings only as a risk. The only market-price evidence is the period-end fair value of the senior notes, stated from observable prices. This leaves Ratings & triggers, Peer benchmark, Market-implied risk and Committee decision without their inputs, and leaves pricing open.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tpc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 34, 47

Board and ownership detail is incomplete. Directors, executive pay and beneficial ownership are incorporated by reference to a proxy statement that is not supplied, so Business & governance rests on the business description, the risk factors and the related-party note.

The 2025 interim comparatives come only from the 2026 quarterly reports, which state that certain prior-year amounts were reclassified. No separately filed 2025 quarterly report is supplied to test them, and the fourth quarter of 2025 has to be derived by subtracting the nine-month figures from the full-year figures.

No numerical conflict was found between the filings in the figures checked: year-end 2025 and 2024 balances, fiscal 2024 revenue, year-end backlog, the cash split and the debt components agree, and the only difference is rounding in the backlog.
Basis: calculation C2; calculation C3; calculation C4; calculation C5; calculation C6; calculation C7; calculation C8; calculation C9

## Request

Financial foundation for Tutor Perini Corp (tpc-77543), as of 2026-11-18, on the credit snapshot pathway. Scope: statements, debt, cash, leverage and interest cover from the 2024 and 2025 annual reports and the three 2026 quarterly reports, in US dollars.

## Findings
### Bottom line

Debt is modest against earnings and covered by cash, but the cushion is thinner than the headline suggests. Gross debt at 2026-09-30 is 1.02x last-twelve-months EBITDA built from statement lines, net debt is below zero, and USD 504,218 thousand of the USD 1,111,049 thousand reported cash is available for general corporate purposes, the rest being held for joint ventures.

FY2024 EBITDA was negative, so leverage that year is not meaningful, and the 2026 refinancing moved the next large maturity to 2033 with the revolver at USD 350,000 thousand undrawn. Customer billings in excess of costs of USD 2,044,207 thousand are the largest liability line on the balance sheet and would reverse if backlog shrank.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tpc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 3, 10, 14–18; calculation C5; calculation C11
### Key findings

Leverage has fallen from not meaningful to modest as earnings recovered and debt was repaid. On FY2025 EBITDA of USD 281,776 thousand gross debt was 1.45x EBITDA and the company held net cash of 1.16x EBITDA, and on last-twelve-months EBITDA of USD 396,576 thousand at 2026-09-30 gross debt is 1.02x and net cash is 1.78x. Gross debt carrying value fell from USD 534,138 thousand at the end of FY2024 to USD 403,641 thousand at 2026-09-30, while income from construction operations swung from a loss of USD 103,753 thousand in FY2024 to a profit of USD 231,961 thousand in FY2025 and USD 302,336 thousand in the nine months of 2026.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_tpc-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 70–71; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tpc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 2–3, 14; calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C4; calculation C5; calculation C9; calculation C10; calculation C11

Interest cover on the latest full year is comfortable but the latest twelve months cannot be tested. FY2025 EBITDA covered cash interest paid of USD 50,419 thousand by 5.59x, against -0.68x in FY2024 when EBITDA was negative. The 2026 refinancing replaced the 2029 senior notes with the 2033 senior notes at a lower coupon, and the company states annualised cash interest savings of USD 21.0 million; the interim reports state no cash interest paid, so cover at 2026-09-30 is not calculable on the method's definition.

Cash generation is strong but is flattered by customer funding. Operating cash flow was USD 748,065 thousand in FY2025 and USD 665,063 thousand in the nine months of 2026, against capital expenditure of USD 180,854 thousand and USD 91,265 thousand, but billings in excess of costs, the customer advances that fund projects, rose from USD 1,216,623 thousand at the end of FY2024 to USD 1,838,610 thousand at the end of FY2025 and USD 2,044,207 thousand at 2026-09-30. That float is more than five times gross debt and reverses if new awards stop replacing revenue, and backlog of USD 20,353.3 million at 2026-09-30 is below the USD 21.6 billion of a year earlier, so operating cash flow of this size is not a stable base.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_tpc-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 71–72; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tpc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 3–4, 49–50; calculation C15; calculation C16

Liquidity is ample against near-term maturities. Cash available for general corporate purposes of USD 504,218 thousand plus the undrawn USD 350,000 thousand revolver is USD 854,218 thousand, against current maturities of debt of USD 4,563 thousand. Most of the reported cash, USD 606,831 thousand, is joint venture cash available only for joint venture uses, so net debt on consolidated cash overstates what creditors can reach; on general-purpose cash alone the company still has net cash of USD 100,577 thousand, or 0.25x EBITDA.

The issuer's own covenant ratios at 2026-09-30, total net leverage of -0.22x and interest cover of 17.14x, follow credit agreement definitions that are not supplied, so they are not comparable with the figures above. ### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest case against the comfortable reading is the Philadelphia hotel litigation: the court awarded the developer approximately USD 175 million, the company's building subsidiary has appealed, and management describes a material adverse impact as neither probable nor remote, against USD 504,218 thousand of general-purpose cash. A second weakness is the earnings record, since FY2024 EBITDA was negative and FY2025 EBITDA includes USD 150,002 thousand of share-based compensation that moves with the share price.

The view would turn if the award were upheld in full on appeal, if billings in excess of costs fell while backlog shrank, or if cash available for general corporate purposes fell back toward the USD 265,647 thousand of FY2024.

Severity: High. Action: obtain the credit agreement definition and the compliance certificate.
FY2024 EBITDA is negative, so total debt and net debt over EBITDA are not calculable for FY2024. Severity: Low. Action: none needed; the ratio is not meaningful.

Severity: Medium. Action: obtain a ladder at 2026-09-30.

The principal of the equipment financing, mortgages and other indebtedness at 2026-09-30, carrying USD 11,085 thousand in total, is not separately stated, and their legal rank is not stated, so they are left out of the debt stack and the principal total at 2026-09-30 is partial. Prior-year amounts in the 2026 quarterly reports are stated to be reclassified to the current presentation, and no separately filed 2025 quarterly report is supplied, so the 9M 2025 comparatives, the derived fourth quarter of 2025 and the last-twelve-months figures cannot be checked against the originally filed numbers. Severity: Low. Action: obtain the 2025 quarterly reports.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tpc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 5
The balance sheet at 2025-09-30 is not supplied, so nine-month 2025 has no balance-sheet column and leverage at that date is not stated. Severity: Low. Action: none needed.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tpc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 3

The credit agreement and indenture are not supplied, so the covenant definitions behind the issuer's total net leverage ratio and interest coverage ratio, and the lien priority of the revolver against other debt, are known only as the filings summarise them. Severity: Medium. Action: obtain the executed documents.

Performance guarantees and other commitments are disclosed as contingent obligations without amounts, and no factoring or supplier finance programme appears in the 2025 annual report or the third-quarter report, so claims outside debt other than operating leases are not quantified. Severity: Low. Action: obtain surety and guarantee exposure from the issuer.

The third-quarter report states an October 2026 court ruling after the balance-sheet date; it names no amount and no effect on net debt, so it is not blended into period figures. Severity: Low. Action: monitor the appeal.

spans.text: # Business and governance fact pack for Tutor Perini Corp (tpc-77543), as of 2026-11-18
## Request

Business, ownership and governance fact pack for Tutor Perini Corp (tpc-77543), as of 2026-11-18, on the credit snapshot pathway. Scope: what the company does, who owns and controls it, how it funds and distributes cash, and what its history means for creditors, from the 2024 and 2025 annual reports and the three 2026 quarterly reports.
## Sources
| Source | Document | Document date | sha256 | Use |

| 10-K_2024-12-31_tpc-20241231.htm.jsonl | Annual report on Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2024 (dated by signature; the filing date is not stated) | 2025-02-27 | f53be5f07f0e8f974583a80cc32e96e4e8fcd60c7ef3672c82cc31a2afc31843 | Business history, 2024 credit agreement and covenant amendments, 2024 financing events |

| 10-K_2025-12-31_tpc-20251231.htm.jsonl | Annual report on Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2025 (dated by signature; the filing date is not stated) | 2026-02-26 | 2cd5d1a91e6ea242529726c39a5cc3947e525e50cd709ef1e8528d1c841efb3f | Business description, risk factors, ownership and related-party disclosures, segment and customer data, exhibits, governance and capital allocation |

| 10-Q_2026-03-31_tpc-20260331.htm.jsonl | Quarterly report on Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2026 (dated by signature; the filing date is not stated) | 2026-05-06 | 72e63616f6a39194b3384be3f452cb8e32da34cf7256a8bcf01a2b683eee79a2 | Cross-check of first-quarter 2026 events and litigation status |

| 10-Q_2026-06-30_tpc-20260630.htm.jsonl | Quarterly report on Form 10-Q for the quarter ended June 30, 2026 (dated by signature; the filing date is not stated) | 2026-08-05 | ace976cc8e3afaa7b3050692ed8dfcb24a0e2168ab95cef7c4fe7851e03293e0 | Share repurchase authorisation, executive agreements and the second-quarter status of the refinancing |

| 10-Q_2026-09-30_tpc-20260930.htm.jsonl | Quarterly report on Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 (dated by signature; the filing date is not stated) | 2026-11-04 | fc218817c026e0f511b131f95512277de8810c874673ace9f034fa4fa0d52878 | Latest operating data, backlog, joint ventures, litigation, 2026 refinancing, pension settlement and capital returns |
Supplied handoff: Source readiness (CP-0), sha256 372cb0234ef72f339decfbd4a554ed7c19ee307db8e15beaed5f136096ddf7e6, used for the source inventory, perimeter and recorded limitations.
## Findings
### Bottom line

Tutor Perini is a public-company contractor whose creditors depend on project execution and public customers, not on a sponsor, and the filings document no creditor-adverse conduct, though the debt documents that would show what owners may take out are not supplied.

Public agencies were 74.69% of FY2025 revenue and fixed-price work is 79% of backlog, so margins turn on execution and on settling change orders. One holder, the executive chairman with three trusts, owns about 12% and may nominate a director; distributions began in late 2025 and were 6.20% of nine-month 2026 operating cash flow, and the 2026 refinancing cut interest cost.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_tpc-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 11, 27, 85; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tpc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 15; calculation C3; calculation C8
### Key findings

- Revenue visibility is strong but rests on a few large public projects. Backlog of USD 20,353.3 million at 2026-09-30 is about 49% Civil, 35% Building and 16% Specialty Contractors, public agencies made up 86% of backlog at the end of 2025, and a single customer was 10.8% of nine-month 2026 revenue, so a funding delay or a dispute on one project moves earnings. Backlog is down 5.77% on a year earlier, so the cushion is shrinking rather than growing.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tpc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 44, 49–50; 10-K_2025-12-31_tpc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 11; calculation C6; calculation C7; calculation C11

- Margins depend on fixed-price execution and on collecting claims. Fixed-price work is 69.39% of FY2025 revenue and 79% of backlog, customers may terminate government contracts for convenience, and unapproved change orders and claims sit in costs and estimated earnings in excess of billings of USD 767,432 thousand, so a lost claim becomes a cash and earnings shock rather than a delay.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_tpc-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 11, 13, 87; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tpc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 3, 9; calculation C5

- Customer advances and bonding are the funding model, not debt. Billings in excess of costs of USD 2,044,207 thousand fund projects ahead of spending, and surety bonds are needed to win work, so a slowdown in awards or a loss of bonding capacity would hit liquidity before it hits leverage.

- Control is a listed-company board with one influential holder, not a sponsor. The Tutor Group holds about 12% and may nominate one director while it holds at least 11.25%, ten directors signed the annual report, and no fund, fund vintage or exit horizon is described to infer pressure from, so alignment has to be judged from conduct rather than identity.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_tpc-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 27, 65

- Financial policy has moved from covenant relief to returns, and the evidence so far is mixed rather than adverse. Two covenant amendments were needed in 2022 and 2023, the term loan was repaid early in 2025, dividends began in December 2025, USD 30,000 thousand of shares were repurchased in nine months of 2026 with USD 170 million of authorisation left, and the 2026 refinancing cost a USD 35.6 million premium that the issuer-stated USD 21.0 million annual saving repays in 1.70 years.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_tpc-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 26, 52; 10-Q_2026-06-30_tpc-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 67; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tpc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 15, 62, 67; calculation C8; calculation C10; calculation C12

- The Philadelphia hotel dispute is the one live item that could change the picture. The court awarded the developer approximately USD 175 million, the company has appealed, and management describes a material adverse impact as neither probable nor remote.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tpc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 25–26
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against a moderate governance risk reading is the covenant record and the dispute record: the first lien leverage covenant needed two amendments within five months in 2022 and 2023, FY2024 ended in a loss with legacy-dispute charges, and a court awarded approximately USD 175 million, equal to 34.71% of the USD 504,218 thousand of general-purpose cash. The strongest evidence for the opposite, a lower-risk reading, is that distributions were only 6.20% of nine-month 2026 operating cash flow and that the 2026 refinancing lowered interest cost and extended maturity without any documented priming.

The view would worsen if the appeal fails and the award is paid from general-purpose cash, if the indenture or credit agreement prove to allow large restricted payments, or if repurchases accelerate while backlog keeps falling. It would improve if the documents show tight restricted-payment limits and the appeal reduces the award.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_tpc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 26; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tpc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 10, 25–26; calculation C7; calculation C8; calculation C13
### Limitations

- The indenture and credit agreement are not supplied, so restricted-payment, lien and priority capacity cannot be read, and the governance risk level stays at medium instead of moving to low even though no adverse conduct is documented.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tpc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 69

- Directors, their independence, committee roles, executive pay and holders other than the Tutor Group sit in a proxy statement that is not supplied, so the control conclusion rests on one stated holding and a signature page.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_tpc-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 65

- Backlog, new awards and customer concentration are management-defined and unaudited in the quarterly reports, so the revenue-visibility conclusion carries the issuer's own definition of what counts as awarded.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tpc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 49–51
- The amount of unapproved change orders and claims inside costs and estimated earnings in excess of billings is not split out, so the claims-collection risk cannot be sized beyond the total balance.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tpc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 3, 9
### Company and operating model
| Dimension | What the filings state | Why it matters to creditors | Source |

| Business | General contracting, construction management and design-build for public agencies and private customers, with about 1,600 projects in 2025 | Many concurrent projects spread execution risk but each large project can move earnings | 10-K_2025-12-31_tpc-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 4–5 |

| Segments | Civil (heavy civil, tunnels, bridges, transit), Building (healthcare, detention, hospitality and gaming, government) and Specialty Contractors (electrical, mechanical, plumbing, HVAC) | Vertical integration lets the group self-perform work and bid larger projects, and Specialty work is partly for the other two segments | 10-K_2025-12-31_tpc-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 5–10 |

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

The only new debt issue in the period is the refinancing completed on 2026-07-02. The company issued USD 400.0 million of senior unsecured notes due 2033, used the proceeds with cash to redeem in full the USD 400.0 million of senior notes due 2029 at 108.906% of principal, and amended and restated its credit agreement so that the revolver grew from USD 170.0 million to USD 350.0 million with maturity extended to 2031. The old first lien net leverage covenant was replaced by a maximum total net leverage ratio and a minimum interest coverage ratio that apply only to the revolver.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tpc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 15–17

The refinancing cost a loss on extinguishment of USD 51.4 million, of which USD 35.6 million was cash premium and USD 15.8 million was non-cash write-off of unamortised costs, and the company states annualised cash interest savings of USD 21.0 million, so the premium is repaid in 1.70 years if the saving holds. The new notes carry the same subsidiary guarantees as the credit agreement and the revolver stays secured by substantially all assets; the filings describe no change in lien priority and no priming or non-pro-rata step.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tpc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 15–18, 62; calculation C10

Other capital events in the period are not new debt: the remaining term loan was repaid early in the first quarter of 2025, the defined benefit pension plan was settled in the third quarter of 2026 with a USD 33.8 million non-cash charge, and no acquisition, disposal or sponsor transaction is described in any of the five documents.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tpc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 16, 62

spans.text: # Fundamental credit for Tutor Perini Corp (tpc-77543), as of 2026-11-18
## Request

Fundamental credit synthesis for Tutor Perini Corp (tpc-77543), as of 2026-11-18, on the credit snapshot pathway. Scope: business risk, financial profile, outlook, downside and monitoring from the 2024 and 2025 annual reports and the three 2026 quarterly reports, built on the Source readiness, Financial foundation and Business & governance results. No rating, relative-value, recovery or covenant-capacity view is given.

## Findings
### Bottom line

Tutor Perini has an adequate and improving credit profile: gross debt is covered by cash and no debt of size falls due before 2033, so creditors are exposed mainly to fixed-price project execution and one court award, not to refinancing.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tpc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 3, 14–18; calculation C23; calculation C14

At 2026-09-30 gross debt is 1.02x last-twelve-months EBITDA, USD 504,218 thousand of general-purpose cash plus the undrawn USD 350,000 thousand revolver gives USD 854,218 thousand of liquidity, and backlog of USD 20,353.3 million is 3.25x last-twelve-months revenue. The weak points are earnings that were a loss in FY2024 on legal charges, a USD 175 million Philadelphia hotel award under appeal that equals 34.71% of general-purpose cash, and customer advances of USD 2,044,207 thousand that fund the business and would reverse if awards stopped keeping pace with revenue. Awards were 0.96x revenue in the first nine months of 2026, so backlog replacement and claims collection are what to watch.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tpc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 3, 10, 25, 49–50; calculation C23; calculation C14; calculation C7; calculation C17; calculation C24; calculation C6; Financial foundation (CP-1)
### Key findings

The business profile is adequate: large and scaled in work where few firms compete, but concentrated in a handful of big fixed-price public projects. Last-twelve-months revenue is USD 6,254,126 thousand, public agencies were 73.82% of nine-month 2026 revenue, and two customers with multiple projects made up 24.1% of it, at 13.3% and 10.8%; the third-quarter report names the second customer, so the earlier Business & governance figure of one customer at 10.8% understates concentration. Management says fewer firms now bid on the largest civil projects, which helps pricing but cannot be tested because no market-share figure is supplied. A funding delay or a dispute on one large project therefore moves earnings and cash more than the revenue base suggests, so scale is a strength and concentration is the matching weakness.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tpc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 6, 44, 49–50; 10-K_2025-12-31_tpc-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 12, 124; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C7; calculation C8

Revenue is visible for about three years, but the pipeline that feeds it has stopped growing. Nine-month 2026 new awards of USD 4,540.3 million were 0.96x revenue recognised, against USD 7.0 billion in the same period of 2025, and backlog is down 5.77% on a year earlier although up from USD 19.9 billion at the end of the second quarter. Firm remaining performance obligations, which exclude unexercised options, are USD 17.4 billion, 2.78x revenue and down only 2.79% on a year earlier, so the firm base is steadier than the headline backlog. Management attributes the fall to an unusually strong 2025 and fewer large awards reaching decision in 2026, and points to a pipeline above USD 200 billion over three to four years and a multi-billion-dollar California healthcare project to be added within two years; these are expectations, not bookings. Backlog equal to 3.25 years of revenue protects earnings in the near term, but sustained awards below revenue would shrink it and the customer advances attached to it.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tpc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 8, 49–50, 52–53, 58; calculation C6; calculation C7; calculation C9

Margin recovery is real but comes from volume and lower stock-linked pay rather than better gross margins, so it is less secure than the headline suggests. Income from construction operations moved from a margin of -2.40% in FY2024 to 4.18% in FY2025 and 6.37% in the first nine months of 2026, yet gross margin was 12.37% against 12.38% a year earlier; of the USD 120,487 thousand rise in operating income, 72.69% came from higher gross profit on 17.62% more revenue and the rest from lower general and administrative cost as share-based pay fell by USD 43.5 million. Civil earned a 14.0% margin against 4.8% in Building and 2.1% in Specialty Contractors, so Civil execution carries the credit.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tpc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 42–43, 47, 55–60; 10-K_2025-12-31_tpc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 70; calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C3; calculation C4; calculation C5

Disputes are a recurring cost of this business model, not a one-off, and unproven claims decide how much profit turns into cash. Legal judgments and settlements cost USD 213.5 million in FY2024 and USD 94.3 million in FY2025, which is 40.65% of FY2025 income from construction operations, and a USD 16.4 million adverse change on a California transit project in the first quarter of 2026 came from change-order negotiations that management says were later settled with the owner and should bring cash. Fixed-price work was 79% of backlog at the end of 2025, and claims plus unapproved change orders of USD 687,916 thousand are 89.64% of the USD 767,432 thousand of costs in excess of billings and 136.43% of general-purpose cash, with management expecting about USD 521.4 million of that balance to be collected beyond one year, so a lost claim becomes a charge and a delayed collection together. The third-quarter report states this split, which corrects the earlier Business & governance statement that it is not stated.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_tpc-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 11, 32–33; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tpc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 3, 8–9, 56; calculation C18; calculation C10; Business & governance (CP-1A)

Cash generation is strong but partly customer funded, so it should not be capitalised as a stable base. Operating cash flow was USD 665,063 thousand in the first nine months of 2026, of which USD 249,832 thousand came from working-capital inflows, and in FY2024 operating cash flow of USD 503,544 thousand was more than all working capital, since before it the figure was USD -85,580 thousand. After capital expenditure of USD 91,265 thousand the nine-month figure was USD 573,798 thousand, before USD 23,800 thousand paid to joint venture partners and USD 41,202 thousand of dividends and repurchases. Capital intensity is low at 1.92% of revenue, but FY2025 spending of USD 180,854 thousand was 3.26% of revenue and 3.80x depreciation on owner-funded equipment for newer projects, so capital expenditure is flexible but not zero.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_tpc-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 48, 71–72; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tpc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4; calculation C11; calculation C12; calculation C13

Liquidity is strong against every maturity and against the known cash calls, but nearly a quarter of the general-purpose cash is already claimed by share awards. At 2026-09-30 cash available for general corporate purposes of USD 504,218 thousand plus the undrawn USD 350,000 thousand revolver is USD 854,218 thousand, while USD 606,831 thousand, or 54.62% of reported cash, is joint venture cash that creditors cannot count on. Cash-settled share awards are liabilities of USD 120.9 million, up from USD 85.2 million at the end of 2025 even after USD 31.0 million paid in nine months, and equal to 23.98% of general-purpose cash; management says most remaining awards of this kind vest by the end of 2026, and the filings do not say when the cash is paid. The Philadelphia hotel award adds a contingent USD 175 million, or 34.71% of the same cash.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tpc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 3, 10, 25, 28, 61; 10-K_2025-12-31_tpc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 108; calculation C14; calculation C15; calculation C16; calculation C28; calculation C17

Financial policy has shifted from repair to returns, which is acceptable at this leverage but has not been tested by a downturn. The first lien leverage covenant needed two amendments in 2022 and 2023 and FY2024 ended in a loss; since then the term loan was repaid early, dividends began in December 2025 and USD 30,000 thousand of shares were bought back, leaving USD 170 million of authorisation. Returns were 6.20% of nine-month operating cash flow and gross debt is 22.69% of total capitalisation; no sponsor sits above the company, the executive chairman and related trusts hold about 12% and may nominate a director, and alignment therefore has to be judged from conduct, which so far shows returns well below operating cash flow.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_tpc-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 26–27, 52; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tpc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 67; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C21; calculation C22

Refinancing risk is low until 2031, and the one market price supplied does not signal distress, though it is below par. The July 2026 refinancing replaced the 2029 notes with USD 400.0 million of senior unsecured notes due 2033 and lifted the secured revolver to USD 350.0 million, undrawn and maturing in 2031, at a cash premium of USD 35.6 million that the issuer-stated USD 21.0 million of annual interest saving repays in 1.70 years; management also states that interest income exceeded interest expense from the third quarter of 2026 and expects that to continue. The 2033 notes were valued at USD 390.0 million, or 97.50% of principal, at 2026-09-30, which implies a yield above the coupon, and no peer prices are supplied to say whether that is wide; the revolver's two maintenance tests, reported at -0.22x against a 3.50x maximum and 17.14x against a 3.00x minimum, apply only to the revolver and follow definitions that are not supplied.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tpc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 15–18, 34, 62, 66; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C25; calculation C26; calculation C27
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against an adequate and improving view is that the improvement is recent and leans on items that may not repeat: FY2024 EBITDA was negative, 44.20% of FY2025 operating cash flow came from working-capital inflows, awards are below revenue, legal and settlement charges have recurred in both years, and the Philadelphia award equals 44.13% of last-twelve-months EBITDA. The strongest evidence for a better view than adequate is that consolidated net debt is -1.78x EBITDA, general-purpose cash alone exceeds gross debt, and a cash call of USD 337,900 thousand from the award, the window wall ruling and the share awards would still leave USD 516,318 thousand of liquidity.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tpc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 3, 25–28, 49–50; 10-K_2025-12-31_tpc-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 32–33, 71; calculation C11; calculation C6; calculation C18; calculation C17; calculation C23; calculation C19

The view would worsen if the appeal fails while awards stay below revenue and billings in excess of costs start to fall, if unapproved change orders are written down, or if repurchases accelerate while backlog shrinks. It would improve if awards exceed revenue for several quarters, the appeal cuts the award, claims on the California transit and other projects convert to cash, and the debt documents show tight limits on payouts.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tpc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 3, 8, 25–26, 28, 49–50; calculation C6; calculation C10; calculation C17
### Limitations

- No agency rating, peer set or dated bond quote beyond one period-end fair value is supplied, so the adequate business-profile conclusion is absolute rather than relative to other contractors and the financial-policy and refinancing conclusions cannot be calibrated against how the market prices comparable credit.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tpc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 34

- The amount of recovery carried in receivables for the Philadelphia hotel project is not stated, so the earnings effect of losing the appeal cannot be separated from the cash payment, and the downside case treats the full award as cash only.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tpc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 25–26

- Dates for paying the cash-settled share awards and any appeal bond or collateral needed to stay the Philadelphia award are not stated, so the timing of the largest known cash calls in the downside case is an assumption.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tpc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 26, 28

- The pipeline above USD 200 billion and the timing of the California healthcare project are management expectations without dates or probabilities, so the medium-term outlook leans on language the filings do not evidence and is held at adequate rather than strong.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tpc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 52–53

- The leverage and cover figures use EBITDA built after stock-linked pay and the covenant ratios use definitions that are not supplied, so the financial-profile conclusion could move by the size of the stock-linked charge, which was USD 77,179 thousand in nine months.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tpc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 66; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C29
### Strengths and weaknesses

Strength: net cash and a long maturity profile. At 2026-09-30 gross debt of USD 403,641 thousand is 1.02x last-twelve-months EBITDA and 22.69% of total capitalisation, general-purpose cash of USD 504,218 thousand exceeds it, and the only large maturity is the 2033 notes, so over the next two years default would have to come from execution and litigation losses rather than from a debt wall, and a refinancing is not needed to stay liquid.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tpc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 3, 10, 14–18; calculation C23; calculation C22; calculation C14

Strength: contracted, publicly funded backlog. Backlog of USD 20,353.3 million is 3.25 years of revenue and firm obligations are 2.78x, public agencies were 73.82% of nine-month 2026 revenue and Civil carries a 14.0% margin, so revenue and the most profitable segment are visible for about three years, which supports debt service even if new awards slow for a few quarters.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tpc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 6, 8, 49–50, 55–56; calculation C7; calculation C9; calculation C5

Strength: lower fixed charges and light covenants. The 2026 refinancing cut interest expense to USD 34,407 thousand for nine months from USD 41,489 thousand, the issuer-stated annual saving is USD 21.0 million, management states that interest income has exceeded interest expense since the third quarter of 2026, and the only maintenance tests apply to an undrawn revolver, so fixed charges and default triggers are lower than a year ago and a covenant breach is a remote route to default.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tpc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 15–18, 62, 66; calculation C26; calculation C27

Strength: improving earnings power in the largest segment. Operating margin reached 6.37% in nine months against -2.40% in FY2024, driven by volume on larger projects, so earnings, not asset sales, are building the cash that covers the debt.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tpc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 55–56; calculation C2; calculation C4

Weakness: fixed-price execution and recurring disputes. Fixed-price work was 79% of backlog at the end of 2025, legal judgments and settlements cost USD 213.5 million in FY2024 and USD 94.3 million in FY2025, and claims plus unapproved change orders of USD 687,916 thousand exceed general-purpose cash, so overruns and lost claims fall on the company and a single dispute can swing a year, as a USD 101.6 million adjustment for an arbitration ruling on a completed California bridge project did in FY2024, which makes earnings the least predictable part of the credit.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_tpc-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 11, 32–33, 86; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tpc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 8; calculation C18; calculation C10

Weakness: the Philadelphia hotel award. The court awarded about USD 175 million, 34.71% of general-purpose cash and 44.13% of last-twelve-months EBITDA, a second ruling adds USD 42 million, and in October 2026, after the balance sheet date, the trial court denied the company's indemnity claims against its concrete subcontractor and that subcontractor's surety, which narrows the recovery available, so a loss on appeal would be the largest single contingent cash call in the filings, fundable from cash but large enough to change how much room remains for returns and projects.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tpc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 25–26; calculation C17

Weakness: customer-funded working capital. Billings in excess of costs of USD 2,044,207 thousand are 5.06x gross debt and 37.57% of nine-month operating cash flow came from working capital, so cash generation depends on advances that reverse if awards stop replacing revenue, and a return of advances outside the joint ventures to their end-2024 level would absorb USD 587,370 thousand.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tpc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 3, 4; 10-K_2025-12-31_tpc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 71; calculation C24; calculation C11; calculation C20

Weakness: slowing backlog replacement and unsettled funding. Awards were 0.96x revenue, backlog is down 5.77% on a year earlier, and the federal infrastructure funding window closed on 2026-09-30 with authorisations extended only to 2026-12-11, so growth in visibility is not assured and the sector tailwind depends on legislation not yet passed.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tpc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 49–50, 53; calculation C6; calculation C7

Weakness: financial policy that depends on documents not seen. Cash-settled share awards of USD 120.9 million, a USD 170 million repurchase authorisation and an executive chairman with about 12% and a board nomination right all compete for the same cash, and without the executed debt documents the limit on payouts cannot be read, so the policy dimension is held at average.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tpc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 28, 67; 10-K_2025-12-31_tpc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 27; calculation C16; calculation C21; Business & governance (CP-1A)
### Outlook, tailwinds and headwinds

Over the next one to two years earnings should hold or improve while cash is drawn on by known items. The large projects now in execution have substantial scope remaining, backlog rose from USD 19.9 billion at the end of the second quarter to USD 20,353.3 million, annual cash interest is expected to fall by the issuer-stated USD 21.0 million, and management projects lower stock-linked pay in 2026 and a much larger fall in 2027. Against that, the Philadelphia appeal, the share award settlements and the repurchase authorisation of USD 170 million could all draw on the same USD 504,218 thousand of general-purpose cash, so liquidity should stay ample but shrink before it grows.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tpc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 25–28, 47–50, 61–62, 67; calculation C7; calculation C26; calculation C16; calculation C14

Over three to five years the outlook turns on funding that is not settled. The federal infrastructure law funding window closed on 2026-09-30 and surface-transportation authorisations were extended only to 2026-12-11 while a USD 580 billion reauthorisation bill is negotiated; management states that most major projects rely more on state and local funding, cites USD 41.4 billion of voter-approved transportation measures from November 2024, and points to defence funding in Guam and the Indo-Pacific. These are management statements and the filings give no probability or timing for reauthorisation, so a funding gap would first show as slower awards and shrinking customer advances rather than as a debt problem.

Competitive and cost forces matter to creditors mainly through bidding and margin. Management says few firms bid on the largest fixed-price civil projects, which supports awards and pricing, while customers are mostly public agencies that can end contracts for convenience and buy by competitive bid, so buyer power is high on smaller jobs and lower on the largest. Cost inflation and tariffs are managed by buying out materials, taking fixed-price quotes from subcontractors and pricing escalation into bids, which shifts much of the risk to suppliers but not all of it; about 4,000 employees are union members with wage escalation priced into bids. Technology and social factors do not appear to be a primary credit driver based on the provided materials.
### Downside scenario

The realistic downside is a loss on the Philadelphia appeal combined with awards that stay below revenue, which hits cash before it hits leverage. First, the court award of about USD 175 million and the USD 42 million window wall ruling are upheld and the share awards settle in cash, a cash call of USD 337,900 thousand that leaves USD 166,318 thousand of general-purpose cash and USD 516,318 thousand of liquidity with the revolver, and net debt on general-purpose cash of USD 237,323 thousand, or 0.60x last-twelve-months EBITDA. Second, awards below revenue stop the growth of customer advances; a return of the advances outside joint ventures to their end-2024 level would absorb a further USD 587,370 thousand, 68.76% of the original liquidity, which together with the first call, USD 925,270 thousand, would exceed the original USD 854,218 thousand of liquidity, but that needs several years of shrinking awards and is the tail, not the base case.

Revenue would not fall quickly because backlog covers about three years, and margins would be pressured by further adverse adjustments like the USD 16.4 million recorded in the first quarter of 2026 and by the loss of the recovery carried on the hotel project. Management levers are the undrawn revolver, the discretionary repurchase authorisation, dividends of USD 5.0 million declared in the third quarter, the timing of equipment purchases and distributions to joint venture partners. Resilience looks sufficient to avoid liquidity distress in the first case; distress needs the combined tail, and the covenants apply only to the revolver, so a breach would first affect revolver access, and whether it would reach the notes depends on cross-default terms that are not supplied. Each 10% of claims and unapproved change orders that is not collected would cost USD 68,792 thousand of earnings and cash. These figures are arithmetic on stated amounts, not a forecast.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tpc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 3, 4, 10, 25–28, 49–50, 56, 67; 10-K_2025-12-31_tpc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 71; calculation C19; calculation C20; calculation C16; calculation C17; calculation C10
### Overall credit view

Overall, Tutor Perini presents an adequate business profile supported by a USD 20,353.3 million backlog, public customers and a refinanced balance sheet, but credit quality is constrained by fixed-price execution risk, recurring dispute charges and customer-funded working capital. Cash-flow durability appears adequate because operating cash flow before working capital was USD 415,231 thousand in nine months, although it is flattered by customer advances that cannot be assumed to grow. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on earnings holding near current levels and on bond market access as the 2033 notes approach maturity, since nothing of size matures sooner. The primary downside path is a loss on the Philadelphia appeal combined with awards below revenue and shrinking customer advances. Further analysis would require the executed debt documents, the covenant definitions, the collection timetable for claims and unapproved change orders, the recovery carried on the hotel project and market prices for comparison. The top risk is backlog replacement failing while claims remain uncollected.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tpc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 3, 25–26, 49–50, 66; calculation C11; calculation C7; calculation C24; calculation C17; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)
